verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents built-in internal status pages "meant for the internal team only", with a dedicated ephemeral page per incident, which covers the employee-only audience. Access control is only implied: the docs say pages for organization-public incidents need no auth, suggesting private incidents are gated. External status pages exist, but nothing shows private or customer-specific external pages with audience access control. Missing for 10: documented access controls (auth, SSO gating, allowlists) for status pages, private customer-specific status pages, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering leader, I can run private or internal status pages with access control for customer-specific or employee-only audiences

citations.quote: The FireHydrant platform offers both internal status pages, which are meant for the internal team only and require no setup
For public (to your organization) incidents, these internal status pages do not require auth or a FireHydrant license to view.
each incident on FireHydrant will have a dedicated ephemeral status page that summarizes high-level details and includes key links.
